subject: GLOBAL clause
notes: kb/Work PB1045 (wave 1032 E). Rule: "The GLOBAL clause shall not be specified in a factory definition, an instance definition, or a method definition." (cite.py --check 13.18.27.3 -> OK §13.18.27.3 4)). ONE reporter: OoDefinitionRules.Screen, called for every factory, instance and method data division (a method prototype of an interface included; cite.py --check 10.6.1 'A method-definition in an interface-definition defines a method prototype' -> OK), walks the WRITTEN data division for every GLOBAL clause over GlobalClauseSites - the grammar rules that carry it, which are SR1's entry kinds a) constant, b) data description, d) file description, e) report description (c) has no grammar site: the screen module is declined, COBOL1560) - and reports COBOL1520 (DiagnosticCatalog.GlobalInOoDefinition) at the clause, naming the entry. OoDefinitionRulesDriftTests holds GlobalClauseSites equal to the parser rules whose ATN matches the GLOBAL token less useStatement (the USE GLOBAL phrase), so a GLOBAL clause added to the grammar joins SR4. PROBES on the w1032e build: `01 KC CONSTANT IS GLOBAL AS 5` in a class OBJECT, a FACTORY constant, a method LOCAL-STORAGE constant and an interface prototype's LINKAGE constant each compiled clean before and draw COBOL1520 after; a TYPEDEF GLOBAL in object/factory working storage (never in CallGlobalRoots) is now refused too; files, reports and level-1 data items keep their refusal (FactoryFile/ObjectFile/ObjectReport/ObjectData/MethodData_Global_1520).
